data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication is exactly 23, and the stall is explained by a symmetry obstruction: the isotropy group of the `<3,3,3>` tensor cannot support a rank-22 decomposition without violating intrinsic dimension constraints of its algebraic variety.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A rank-22 decomposition is found and sandbox-verified by integer arithmetic over the 729 tensor entries.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"An exhaustive search over a symmetry-restricted class of rank-22 candidates discovers a valid construction.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The structural obstruction lemma is refuted at a smaller decidable format (e.g., finding that an equivalent obstruction does not prevent rank reduction for `<2,2,2>`).","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The `<3,3,3>` tensor possesses a large isotropy group. A rank-22 decomposition requires 22 rank-1 tensors whose sum equals the target tensor. The kernels of the flattening matrices of these rank-1 components must intersect in a way constrained by the tensor rank. For rank 22, the required dimension of the kernel intersection drops below the minimal orbit dimension allowable by the symmetry group. Thus, any valid 22-decomposition would have to be highly asymmetric, violating the tensor's intrinsic algebraic variety and rendering the decomposition impossible.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
